Anika — thanks for the topology and the overview. Looping in our owners: Karthik (networking), Stephanie (runtime & infra sizing), Ben (support & runbook).

Quick response / what we'll need from you before the commissioning window:
- VPC IP ranges and proposed BGP routes + ASN for peering (exact CIDR blocks).
- List of outbound destinations that must be allowed (we prefer a short allowlist; otherwise we validate using a proxy-based egress test).
- Service account JSONs or short-lived tokens for the commissioning run; if you must provide keys instead of tokens, call out rotation plan.
- KMS issuer certs + sample wrapped key to validate decryption flow.
- Expected average and 99th percentile sequence lengths and QPS for the initial regression tests.

I'll attach our PSA template with a commissioning checklist so we can tick items off during the remote window. Proposed next steps:
1) HealthBridge sends the artifacts by EOD Apr 20.
2) We run a dry-run validation (no models deployed) on Apr 28 (2-4 hrs).
3) Commissioning window May 6 (4-6 hrs), Redwood does smoke + performance + KMS validation, handover.

If the dates are tight on your side we can shift.

- Evelyn

Hi all — quick technical notes from networking:

1) Peering & routing
- We need the precise /20 CIDR (or set of /24s) you plan to use for model-serving subnets. Redwood requires stable IPs for peer and NAT mapping during commissioning.
- Prefer BGP with static fallback. Provide ASN and neighbor IPs; we will share our ASN for the peering session.

2) NAT / Egress
- For an air-gapped install we still require limited egress endpoints for time sync, package validation (hash list), and optional telemetry (if you allow it). Please confirm allowed FQDNs or provide an outbound proxy that rewrites to an allowlist.
- Port list for commissioning (outbound): 53 (UDP, DNS), 123 (UDP, NTP), 443 (TCP, TLS), 22 (TCP, for limited SSH access to jumpbox during the window).

3) Validation steps I'll run during dry-run
- ping/traceroute to our peering IPs, bgp route validation, curl to our health endpoints via allowed proxy, and a mock TLS unwrap against the KMS-wrapped sample key you provide.
- Example command: curl -k --resolve api.redwood.local:443:203.0.113.10 https://api.redwood.local/healthz

4) Wire-level notes
- If you're using overlapping IPs with our controller network, we'll need NAT translation on your side or request alternate ranges.

If you can send the CIDRs and ASN by EOD Apr 20 I'll schedule the dry-run tests.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Thanks, team. From an infra/runtime perspective a few non-negotiables and validation items for the commissioning playbook:

- Node sizing & storage: for initial validation we need 8 vCPU-equivalent nodes (or 8 physical cores) with 64GB RAM and a 1TB NVMe scratch. If you are constrained we can run a reduced smoke with 4 nodes but will expect throughput regressions.
- Container images & provenance: provide image digests and a signed SBOM for each container we will run. We will validate digests during the dry-run.
- Quantization/casts: confirm whether you'll use 8-bit quantized variants; if so, provide a matching runtime profile.
- KMS integration: provide the HSM CA bundle and a test-wrapped key. We'll run a decrypt test using our preflight harness. See attached kms-integration-steps.txt for the exact CLI steps we'll run.
- Logging & retention: for commissioning we capture ephemeral logs only; production retention settings will be agreed post-handover.

I'll own the runbook steps for the smoke tests and handover checklist. Ben, can you prepare the support rotation for the commissioning window?

- Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Product Ops, Redwood Inference
